Upload artifacts to a repository

Upload artifacts to a Repsy repository: rp push &lt;format&gt; &lt;file&gt;... --repo &lt;name&gt;.

The credential is the one rp uses everywhere: REPSY_TOKEN, else the stored
credential of the profile. It is sent as the password of HTTP basic
authentication, so it must be a deploy token of the repository or a personal
access token; a login session cannot upload. Files are streamed from disk and
sent once; rp never retries an upload. If the server refuses it (a plan quota,
a size limit, a duplicate version), its answer is shown as sent.

Docker (rp push docker &lt;archive-or-layout&gt; --repo &lt;name&gt;) is the exception to
"files, basic authentication, one request": the registry wants the token
exchange and one request per blob, and the input is an image archive (docker save,
tar, tar.gz) or an OCI layout directory, with no Docker daemon. A blob that
breaks in transit continues where the registry stopped; a layer the registry
already holds is skipped.

```
rp push
```
